metaData.originalTitle: British Columbia， Time Zones， and Postgres | Crunchy Data Blog
metaData.title: British Columbia， Time Zones， and Postgres | Crunchy Data Blog
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article uses British Columbia's 2026 permanent switch to Pacific Daylight Time as a case study to expose how PostgreSQL's `timestamptz` can silently corrupt future local times and proposes a dual-column schema pattern to preserve user intent.
metaData.summary: When British Columbia stopped observing standard time in March 2026, any PostgreSQL database using `timestamptz` columns for future appointments in the America/Vancouver timezone became vulnerable to hour-off errors. The article explains that `timestamptz` stores UTC at insert time and converts back to local time using the current `tzdata` rules at query time. If `tzdata` updates after the policy change, queries return different local times than what users originally entered. The author demonstrates the problem with a concrete example (a 10 AM appointment shifting to 11 AM) and then presents a three-column schema: a bare `timestamp` for local time, a `text` column for the IANA timezone, and a calculated `timestamptz` column for UTC. A trigger recomputes the UTC value on insert/update, and a simple `UPDATE` can recalculate all future rows after a `tzdata` update. The article also discusses RFC 9557, noting it explicitly avoids solving this problem, and outlines steps to recover if the `tzdata` package has already been upgraded. The author cautions against over-engineering—the dual-column pattern is justified only when local intent is authoritative.

mainPoints.point: Storing future local times as `timestamptz` breaks when timezone rules change after storage.
mainPoints.explanation: `timestamptz` converts to UTC at insert time using then-current rules, and converts back at query time using current rules. A rule change between storage and retrieval shifts the local display, misleading users.

mainPoints.point: A dual-column pattern preserves the user's original wall-clock intent.
mainPoints.explanation: Store the wall-clock value (`timestamp`) and IANA timezone name (`text`) separately; derive a UTC `timestamptz` column via trigger for indexing and queries. This allows recalculation of UTC when `tzdata` is updated.

mainPoints.point: RFC 9557 explicitly does not solve this problem, so a dual-column approach remains necessary.
mainPoints.explanation: RFC 9557 adds timezone info to timestamps but states it is not meant to handle future changes in timezone definitions that affect the instant represented.

mainPoints.point: If `tzdata` has already been upgraded, a careful migration plan is needed.
mainPoints.explanation: Identify rows impacted after the update, notify users, run a non-production test, then apply a targeted `UPDATE` to recalculate UTC values for future appointments.

keyQuotes: If you stored timestamps in a UTC-based column for British Columbia-based appointment in 2026 and beyond, your November through March appointments may be off by an hour!
The dual-column pattern is necessary when the local intent is authoritative: people or deliveries at a time and place, legal deadlines, calendar events, etc.
Don't go overboard though. When the event is in the past, or the exact UTC moment is authoritative (log entries, financial transactions, sensor readings), use plain timestamptz.

relatedArticles.title: How Instacart Built a Search for Billions of Products
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Instacart evolved its search infrastructure from Elasticsearch to Postgres and then to a unified pgvector-based system, achieving a 10x reduction in write workload and a 6% drop in zero-result searches by co-locating data and compute.

relatedArticles.title: Applying Best Simple System for Now for Software Design
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Daniel Terhorst-North argues that programmers should design the 'Best Simple System for Now' (BSSN), focusing on immediate requirements without speculative complexity, to achieve continuous shippability and easier future changes.

relatedArticles.title: Software Architecture Guide
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This page from Martin Fowler presents his perspective on software architecture, defining it as the important stuff in system design, and serves as a curated guide to his site's extensive resources on application and enterprise architecture.

relatedArticles.title: Xiaomi MiMo， Explore and Love
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Xiaomi MiMo and TileRT achieve 1000+ tokens/s inference on a 1-trillion-parameter model using commodity GPUs through extreme model-system codesign, including FP4 quantization and DFlash speculative decoding.

relatedArticles.title: Fintech Engineering Handbook
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This handbook provides a comprehensive set of engineering patterns for building trustworthy financial systems, covering money representation, ledger recording, and execution flows.

relatedArticles.title: Escaping the Fork: How Meta Modernized WebRTC Across 50+ Use Cases
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Meta details their multiyear engineering effort to migrate from a legacy, heavily-forked WebRTC implementation to a modern, upstream-aligned architecture using a dual-stack shim layer and automated feature branching.

relatedArticles.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI engineers detail a five-month experiment building a production software product with zero manually-written code, using Codex agents to achieve 10x velocity and redefining the engineer's role as system designer and feedback loop architect.

relatedArticles.title: Dario Amodei — Policy on the AI Exponential
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Dario Amodei argues that AI is advancing exponentially, creating a dangerous mismatch with slow-moving policy, and proposes concrete actions across regulation, economics, science, civil liberties, and geopolitics to meet the moment.

relatedArticles.title: Inside FAISS: Billion-Scale Similarity Search
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep, visual, and intuitive explanation of FAISS, covering the core ideas of IVF, Product Quantization, their combination in IVFPQ, and GPU acceleration, to enable billion-scale similarity search.

relatedArticles.title: Agentic Code Review
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: As AI agents generate code at machine speed, the bottleneck in software engineering has shifted from writing code to reviewing it, making code review the most leveraged skill and requiring a fundamental rethinking of how review is done.
